question: What best describes what starts human labor?

options.A: A mix of signals from both mother and baby
options.B: A single chemical released by the placenta
options.C: Complete physical exhaustion of the pregnant woman
options.D: An abrupt drop in maternal blood pressure

explanation: Labor starts through a teamwork of chemical and physical signals passing between the mother and the fetus rather than a single event. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is the exact start of human labor still studied closely?

options.A: Because pregnant women rarely show signs before contractions begin
options.B: Because it involves multiple body systems working together
options.C: Because no hormones change during late pregnancy
options.D: Because modern ultrasound cannot detect uterine activity

explanation: Labor initiation involves the hormonal, mechanical, and nervous systems working together at the same time. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which gland in the baby matures near term to help start labor?
explanation: The fetal adrenal glands produce cortisol near term, signaling the placenta to change hormone production and start labor. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of progesterone during most of the pregnancy?

options.B: Keeping the uterine muscle relaxed and quiet
options.C: Increasing the blood pressure of the mother
options.D: Softening and opening up the cervix early

explanation: Progesterone acts as a natural relaxant for the uterus, preventing early birth until its levels drop at term. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h2)

question: What do prostaglandins do to the cervix before labor?
explanation: Prostaglandins break down fibers in the cervix, allowing it to soften and open up for childbirth. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h3)

question: How do prostaglandins help oxytocin during delivery?

options.A: By cooling down the temperature of the pelvis
options.B: By stopping blood flow to the lower uterine segment
options.C: By neutralizing oxytocin to prevent over-contraction
options.D: By making the uterine muscle cells more sensitive to contractions

explanation: Prostaglandins prepare the uterine muscle so that oxytocin can trigger stronger and more coordinated contractions. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h3)

question: What are gap junctions in the pregnant uterus?

options.A: Blood vessels that supply nutrients to the fetus
options.B: Specialized connections that help uterine muscle cells contract together
options.C: Empty spaces between the placenta and uterine wall
options.D: Ligaments holding the uterus to the pelvic bones

explanation: Gap junctions form pathways between muscle cells so the uterus can contract as a single strong unit during labor. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why do oxytocin receptors increase on the uterine muscle just before labor?

options.A: To block pain signals traveling to the maternal brain
options.B: To ensure the uterus responds strongly to hormonal signals
options.C: To keep the placenta firmly attached to the uterine lining
options.D: To prevent the baby from moving down too quickly

explanation: An increase in oxytocin receptors primes the uterus to react powerfully to circulating oxytocin when labor begins. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h4)

question: What does the uterine stretch theory suggest about the start of labor?

options.A: Complete lack of movement from the fetus
options.B: Sudden cooling of amniotic fluid inside the sac
options.C: Dehydration of the pregnant woman's tissues
options.D: Extreme stretching of muscle fibers makes them contract

explanation: When uterine muscle fibers stretch to their maximum capacity near term, they respond by generating contractions. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h5)

question: What happens during Ferguson's reflex when the baby's head presses on the cervix?

options.A: Blood pressure drops rapidly in the mother
options.B: Progesterone production increases in the placenta
options.C: The cervix instantly closes to protect the fetus
options.D: Oxytocin is released to cause stronger contractions

explanation: Pressure on the cervix stimulates nerve pathways that prompt the brain to release oxytocin, intensifying labor contractions. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is knowing how labor starts important when managing a post-date pregnancy in a clinic?

options.A: It eliminates the need to monitor fetal heart sounds during contractions
options.B: It helps the midwife calculate the exact baby weight using a tape measure
options.C: It guides decisions on when and how to safely use medical induction methods
options.D: It ensures the mother avoids eating traditional foods during early labor

explanation: Understanding hormonal and mechanical triggers helps midwives choose appropriate interventions like prostaglandins when labor fails to start naturally. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a practical benefit of understanding labor physiology for a midwife?

options.A: Providing safe care during induced or augmented labor
options.B: Predicting the exact second a baby will be born without examination
options.C: Explaining the birth process simply to anxious family members
options.D: Recognizing why certain drugs like oxytocin work on the uterus

explanation: While physiological knowledge helps manage labor, it is impossible to predict the exact moment of birth with second-by-second accuracy. [learn more](BMP212_U2_T1#BMP212_U2_T1_h6)
